explanation: There is no religious or cultural taboo against using the left hand in the Netherlands, unlike in parts of South Asia, the Middle East, or North Africa. Most Dutch people simply follow continental European table manners — fork in the left hand, knife in the right — regardless of which hand they naturally favor.
local_tip: Feel free to use either hand; if you want to match local table manners, hold your fork in your left hand and knife in your right while cutting.

also_check.note: The left hand is considered unclean in many traditional and religious contexts, so eating or passing food with it can cause offense.
The left hand is traditionally considered unclean and is not used for eating or passing food, especially in traditional settings.
In Muslim-majority areas of Indonesia, the left hand is considered impure for eating.
